A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the microscopic model approach is able to describe the (n,xn), (p,xp) and (α,xα) pre-equilibrium reaction cross sections in the medium-energy regime.
the microscopic approach is a promising tool to investigate (n,xn)-pre-equilibrium reactions in the medium-energy region.

the pre-equilibrium process is dominated by the inelastic scattering of the incident neutrons to the low-lying states in the target, and the in-medium effects on the nucleon-nucleus scattering are essential to reproduce the data for the pre-equilibrium (x) reaction channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the in-medium two-body force is essential to describe pre-equilibrium reactions, and that the in-medium NN interaction is not negligible in this process, in contrast to the case of inelastic (n,n') reactions.

the inelastic processes in pre-equilibrium reactions are not limited to the collective states of the target, as it was assumed in the standard models, but they are extended to a large set of inelastic excitations of the target.

the inelastic scattering cross section for neutron-induced reactions is dominated by collective excitations, while the pre-equilibrium process is only a small contribution to the total reaction cross section.
